title: Shanahan Previews Commanders Matchup, Injury Updates
headline: Deebo Samuel Sr. and Nick Bosa are out, Mike Evans is questionable, and Kaelon Black is expected to play; Shanahan also praised Brock Purdy at length.
summary: Shanahan opened with the injury report. Deebo Samuel Sr., Garret Wallow, Nick Bosa and Marques Sigle are out. Mike Evans, Gracen Halton, Upton Stout, Mykel Williams and a couple of other players are questionable. Williams played in Seattle and seems fine, but Shanahan said anyone with any lingering question gets the questionable tag. Kaelon Black is not on the questionable list, so he is expected to play Monday. Shanahan also said one returning player, whose name was garbled in the captions, could be activated Monday. That player's injury looked bad at first and was expected to cost three weeks, but he is now a full go, and Shanahan called the recovery very impressive. At 5-0, Shanahan said you can't get caught up in the highs and lows, and he recalled the 2015 Falcons' 5-0 start and 8-8 finish. He praised Purdy's consistency, comparing him to Matt Ryan as a quarterback who is 'automatic' running a game plan. He said Purdy plays to win, sometimes at his own risk, and has become more aggressive after a camp against a more aggressive defense. He said he no longer thinks about his Washington ties, and he called the Sebastian Valdez roster decision a gamble that worked out.

topics.detail: At 5-0, Shanahan said you can't get caught up in the emotion of the week. He cited the 2015 Falcons (5-0 start, 8-8 finish) and the 2012 Washington team (3-6, then won the division).
Shanahan said Purdy is more aggressive this year partly because he practiced against a different defense in camp. That forced the offense to work on different throws, and he thinks it helped.

A player whose name is garbled in the captions ("Kirk" and "Juice") is a full go, and the team will know Monday whether he is activated. His recovery was far faster than the three weeks first expected.
Shanahan said Valdez played well enough to make the roster initially. The team gambled on getting him through to the practice squad, and he was glad it worked out.
Shanahan said he no longer thinks about his history in Washington. He spoke well of Dan Quinn and Adam Peters.
